Base: batch-2026-10-11-image-only. Sources: Serapion, Practica dicta breviarium, Venice1497, BSB bsb00061068 scans146–147 (fols71v–72r); Avicenna Canon Lyon1522 fol410r (IA1835057.med.yale.edu scan302) and Milan1473 scan453. Manuscript/edition images inspected directly. No expert palaeographic review.

A is upper-cover inside image002 left-column crop(257,1302,1029,2108), native, no transform, same line labels as original reading. B is upper-cover outside image001 left-column crop(1000,1660,1770,2690), native, no transform; linecount starts with the partial first line. These overlap manuscript images, not additional witnesses. Parent coordinator independently reviewed image002 against edition scan146, confirming sequence, not every character.

B2 [preceding black text] Descriptio elect(uarii) diapipereon
B3 usitata conferentis ad frigus sto(machi) et maciem cor-
B4 p(or)is et febrem q(ua)rtanam et malitiam digestionis
B5 et mundificat humiditatem ex stomacho. cuius
B6 preparatio.

Inside right-column rubric read with source assistance: electuarium diapipereon secundum descriptionem galieni; original tentative diapruni is incorrect. This abbreviated rubric is not a full diplomatic transcription.

Continuous sequence: preparations for women/pregnancy and vomiting blood, diaciminum, explanatory commentary including excessively fine grinding and patient anecdote, familiar diaciminum, Galenic diapipereon and its pepper commentary; outside continues to diapipereon usitata and calamentum. SerapionVIIcapXX has this sequence, AvicennaVsummaItractIII shares cumincommentary but differs in adjacent recipes.

Limits: two uppercover faces inspected; lowercover not compared. Weights, all ingredients and every narrative word remain unverified. Some therapeutic descriptions run in red rubrics in manuscript rather than black prose in print; spelling/wording variations remain. No translation, dating, dependence, recension or novelty claim.
